name: Make.com
description: Connect your own Make.com account to view and run your automation scenarios directly from Webbee -- see scenario status, run one on demand, and control activation, all via your own Make API token.

tools.name: connect_make
tools.description: Connect Make.com by saving your own API token, after checking it actually works. Create the token in Make: avatar (bottom-left) -> Profile -> API tab -> Add token. The account's zone (eu1/eu2/us1/us2) is auto-detected -- you don't need to know it.

api_token.description: Make.com API token -- create it in Make: avatar (bottom-left) -> Profile -> API tab -> Add token.
api_token.title: Api Token

tools.name: disconnect_make
tools.description: Disconnect Make.com: deletes the saved API token and zone. Existing scenarios in your Make account are never touched.

tools.name: get_make_connection
tools.description: Check whether Make.com is currently connected (does not reveal the saved token).

tools.name: list_make_teams
tools.description: List the Make.com teams your connected account belongs to. Needed once to pick which team's scenarios to show -- Make requires a specific team (or organization) scope, it has no single global scenario list.

tools.name: select_team
tools.description: Pick which Make.com team's scenarios to show. Run list_make_teams first to see the available team ids. This is a standing choice -- it stays selected until changed again.

team_id.description: Make team id to scope scenario listing to (see list_make_teams).
team_id.title: Team Id

tools.name: list_scenarios
tools.description: List your Make.com scenarios for the selected team -- name, active/paused/invalid state, and last edit time. Run connect_make and select_team first if you haven't yet.

tools.name: run_scenario
tools.description: Run one of your Make.com scenarios right now, by scenario_id (see list_scenarios). This executes the scenario's real actions in Make immediately -- sending emails, writing to connected apps, etc. There is no dry-run or undo, so this always asks for confirm=true first.

scenario_id.description: Make scenario id to run now (see list_scenarios).
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

confirm.description: Must be true. Running a scenario executes its real actions in Make right now (sending emails, writing to connected apps, etc.) -- there is no dry-run or undo.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: set_scenario_active
tools.description: Activate (turn on/schedule) or deactivate (pause) a Make.com scenario by scenario_id (see list_scenarios). Reversible -- flip it back any time -- so unlike run_scenario this needs no confirmation.

scenario_id.description: Make scenario id to activate/deactivate (see list_scenarios).
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

active.description: True to activate (schedule/turn on) the scenario, False to deactivate (pause) it.
active.title: Active

tools.name: set_outgoing_webhook
tools.description: Save (or clear, with an empty webhook_url) the Make Custom Webhook trigger URL that send_webhook_event will POST to. Get this URL by adding a 'Custom Webhook' module as the first step of a Make scenario and copying its URL. This is independent of connect_make.

webhook_url.description: The Custom Webhook trigger URL copied from a Make scenario (add a 'Custom Webhook' module, copy its URL). Leave empty to remove/disable it.
webhook_url.title: Webhook Url

tools.name: get_outgoing_webhook_status
tools.description: Check whether an outgoing Make webhook URL is configured (does not reveal the URL itself).

tools.name: send_webhook_event
tools.description: Send an event payload to the configured Make webhook right now -- for other Imperal apps/automations to trigger a Make scenario. Run set_outgoing_webhook first if you haven't configured one yet.

payload.description: JSON-serializable payload to POST to the configured Make webhook URL -- shape is whatever the receiving Make scenario expects.
payload.title: Payload

tools.name: get_scenario_blueprint
tools.description: Read a scenario's actual module list (blueprint) -- what each numbered step in the flow is and does, in the same order the Make editor numbers them. This is how to answer 'what is module N' or 'what does the Nth step do'.

draft.description: True for the draft (unsaved editor) version, False for the live/published version. Omit to get Make's own default for this scenario.
draft.title: Draft

BlueprintModule.description:
One module (step) in a scenario's blueprint -- position, app/module
identity, and a short label describing what it is. `position` is
1-based to match how modules are numbered in the Make editor UI, so
'module 7' means the 7th entry here.

`raw_config` is the module's own `mapper` object exactly as Make
stores it -- for AI modules (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini "message
assistant"/"create completion" etc.) this is where the actual prompt
text, assistant/model id, and generation params (temperature, etc.)
live. Exposed verbatim (not reshaped) so nothing is silently dropped
or misinterpreted -- Make's own field names vary per app/module.
BlueprintModule.title: BlueprintModule

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List the app connections in your Make team -- what a scenario's modules actually authenticate as (which account/app each connection is for, and whether it's about to expire).

tools.name: delete_connection
tools.description: Permanently delete a Make connection. Any scenario using it will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Any scenario using this connection will stop working once it's deleted.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: rename_connection
tools.description: Rename a Make connection's display name.

name.description: New display name for the connection.
name.title: Name

tools.name: verify_connection
tools.description: Test whether a Make connection's credentials still work.

tools.name: list_data_stores
tools.description: List the data stores (Make's own key/value storage) in your team, with record counts and size.

tools.name: create_data_store
tools.description: Create a new Make data store (key/value storage a scenario can read/write).

name.description: Name for the new data store.
name.title: Name

data_structure_id.description: Optional data structure id defining the record schema. Omit for a schema-less store.
data_structure_id.title: Data Structure Id

tools.name: delete_data_store
tools.description: Permanently delete a Make data store and all of its records.

confirm.description: Must be true. This permanently deletes all its records.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: list_hooks
tools.description: List the incoming webhooks/mailhooks (Make 'hooks') in your team -- the triggers scenarios listen on, with their URL and whether they're enabled.

tools.name: set_hook_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a Make hook (incoming webhook/mailhook) without deleting it.

enabled.description: True to enable (accept data), False to disable.
enabled.title: Enabled

tools.name: delete_hook
tools.description: Permanently remove a Make hook. Any scenario using it will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Any scenario using this hook will stop working once it's deleted.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: list_incomplete_executions
tools.description: List a scenario's incomplete executions (failed runs held for manual resolution instead of being discarded) -- what failed, when, and whether it's already resolved.

scenario_id.description: Scenario id whose incomplete executions to list.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

status.description: Filter by derived status: resolved, scheduled, inprogress, or unresolved.
status.title: Status

tools.name: retry_incomplete_execution
tools.description: Retry one incomplete (failed) scenario execution after fixing the underlying issue.

tools.name: delete_incomplete_executions
tools.description: Permanently delete one scenario's incomplete executions -- explicit ids, or all=true with confirm=true to clear every one.

scenario_id.description: Scenario id whose incomplete executions to delete.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

dlq_ids.description: Explicit incomplete execution ids to delete. Omit and set all=true to delete every one.
dlq_ids.title: Dlq Ids

all.description: Delete every incomplete execution of this scenario.
all.title: All

tools.name: bulk_set_scenario_active
tools.description: Activate or deactivate SEVERAL Make scenarios in one call by explicit scenario ids.

scenario_ids.description: Explicit Make scenario ids; 1-100, never inferred.
scenario_ids.title: Scenario Ids

active.description: True to activate every listed scenario, False to deactivate.
active.title: Active

tools.name: bulk_run_scenarios
tools.description: Run SEVERAL Make scenarios right now, by explicit scenario ids. Executes real actions in each scenario immediately -- no dry-run, always requires confirm=true.

scenario_ids.description: Explicit Make scenario ids; 1-100, never inferred.
scenario_ids.title: Scenario Ids

confirm.description: Must be true. Runs every listed scenario's real actions right now, with no dry-run or undo.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: bulk_delete_connections
tools.description: Permanently delete SEVERAL Make connections at once, by explicit connection ids. Any scenario using one will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Scenarios using these connections will stop working.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: bulk_delete_hooks
tools.description: Permanently remove SEVERAL Make hooks at once, by explicit hook ids. Any scenario using one will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Scenarios using these hooks will stop working.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: preview_update_blueprint_module
tools.description: Preview changing ONE field inside a module's own settings (its mapper -- e.g. an AI module's prompt text) without writing anything. Shows the current value, the proposed value, and a state token that apply_update_blueprint_module must be given unchanged. Use get_scenario_blueprint's raw_config on the module first to see the exact field names available.

module_id.description: The module's own id from get_scenario_blueprint's module_id field (NOT its 1-based position).
module_id.title: Module Id

field.description: Top-level key inside the module's own settings (raw_config from get_scenario_blueprint) to change -- e.g. 'text' for many AI-app prompt fields. Use the exact key name seen in raw_config.
field.title: Field

draft.description: True to preview against the draft version. Omit for Make's own default.
draft.title: Draft

tools.name: apply_update_blueprint_module
tools.description: Apply a previously previewed change to ONE field inside a module's own settings (e.g. an AI module's prompt text). Re-reads the exact scenario blueprint and refuses to write if it changed since preview.

module_id.description: The module's own id (module_id from get_scenario_blueprint).
module_id.title: Module Id

field.description: Same field name used in preview_update_blueprint_module.
field.title: Field

expected_state_token.description: Exact token from preview_update_blueprint_module. Execution stops if the scenario's blueprint changed since preview.
expected_state_token.title: Expected State Token

draft.description: Must match the draft flag used in preview.
draft.title: Draft

confirmed.description: Set true only if Make reports a first-time-app-in-org confirmation is needed.
confirmed.title: Confirmed

tools.name: create_scenario
tools.description: Create a brand-new, empty Make scenario in a team. You'll still need to add modules via preview_update_blueprint_module/apply_update_blueprint_module or the Make editor -- this just creates the container.

team_id.description: Team to create the scenario in (see list_make_teams/select_team).
team_id.title: Team Id

based_on_template_id.description: Create from an existing Make template id instead of empty, if you have one.
based_on_template_id.title: Based On Template Id

folder_id.description: Optional folder id to file the scenario under.
folder_id.title: Folder Id

confirmed.description: Set true only if Make reports the scenario uses an app new to this org and needs install confirmation.
confirmed.title: Confirmed

tools.name: delete_scenario
tools.description: Delete a Make scenario. Make keeps it recoverable in Trash for 30 days -- use restore_scenario to bring it back within that window.

scenario_id.description: Scenario to delete. Make keeps it recoverable in Trash for 30 days (see restore_scenario).
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

tools.name: restore_scenario
tools.description: Restore a deleted Make scenario from Trash, within Make's 30-day recovery window.

scenario_id.description: Scenario id to restore from Trash (within Make's 30-day window).
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

tools.name: clone_scenario
tools.description: Clone an existing Make scenario -- same modules/connections, a new id and name. Optionally into a different team.

team_id.description: Clone into a different team. Omit to clone into the same team.
team_id.title: Team Id

keep_states.description: Also clone module run-state (e.g. last trigger position). False resets it in the clone.
keep_states.title: Keep States

confirmed.description: Set true only if Make reports a first-time-app-in-org confirmation is needed.
confirmed.title: Confirmed

tools.name: update_scheduling
tools.description: Change how/when a scenario runs (interval, cron, on-demand, etc.) without touching its modules.

scheduling_type.description: Make scheduling type: 'indefinitely' (interval-based), 'immediately' (webhook/instant trigger), 'on-demand', 'cron', or 'daily'/'weekly'/'monthly' per Make's own scheduling model.
scheduling_type.title: Scheduling Type

tools.name: list_buildtime_variables
tools.description: List a scenario's buildtime (installation-time) variables -- the named inputs it was configured with, separate from its runtime data.

scenario_id.description: Scenario whose buildtime (installation-time) variables to read.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

tools.name: set_buildtime_variable
tools.description: Add a new buildtime variable to a scenario, or update an existing one's value.

scenario_id.description: Scenario to set the variable on.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

create_new.description: True to add a brand-new variable name; false to update an existing one.
create_new.title: Create New

tools.name: delete_buildtime_variable
tools.description: Remove a buildtime variable from a scenario.

scenario_id.description: Scenario to remove the variable from.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

tools.name: get_scenario_usage
tools.description: Read a scenario's own operations/data-transfer usage history -- how much of your Make plan quota it has consumed, per day.

scenario_id.description: Scenario whose operations/data-transfer usage to read.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

tools.name: list_scenario_logs
tools.description: List a scenario's own operations/data-transfer usage history -- how much of your Make quota each run consumed, most recent first.

status.description: Filter by outcome: 'success', 'warning', or 'error'. Omit for all.
status.title: Status

limit.description: Max executions to return, newest first.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: get_execution_details
tools.description: Read one scenario execution in full -- its actual outputs, or on failure the error message and which module/app caused it.

execution_id.description: Execution id -- the id field from list_scenario_logs.
execution_id.title: Execution Id

return_schema.description:
Per-run detail -- what a scenario execution actually produced or
why it failed, including which module/app was the cause.
return_schema.title: ExecutionDetails

tools.name: stop_execution
tools.description: Stop a currently-running scenario execution.

execution_id.description: Execution id to stop -- must currently be running.
execution_id.title: Execution Id

force.description: True to terminate immediately instead of waiting for the current module to finish.
force.title: Force

tools.name: preview_add_blueprint_module
tools.description: Preview adding a brand-new module to a scenario's flow, without writing anything. Shows where it will land and a state token that apply_add_blueprint_module must be given unchanged. Use get_scenario_blueprint on a similar existing module first to see the exact app_module id and mapper shape to copy.

app_module.description: Make's own app:module id, e.g. 'openai-gpt-3:messageAssistantAdvanced' or 'builtin:BasicRouter'. Copy this from an existing similar module's `module` field in get_scenario_blueprint.
app_module.title: App Module

mapper.description: The new module's settings (its mapper) -- same shape as raw_config on an existing module of the same app_module.
mapper.title: Mapper

after_module_id.description: Insert immediately after this existing module's id. Omit to append at the end of the main flow.
after_module_id.title: After Module Id

draft.description: True to preview against the draft version.
draft.title: Draft

tools.name: apply_add_blueprint_module
tools.description: Apply a previously previewed new module addition to a scenario. Re-reads the exact scenario blueprint and refuses to write if it changed since preview.

expected_state_token.description: Exact token from preview_add_blueprint_module. Refuses to write if the blueprint changed since preview.
expected_state_token.title: Expected State Token

tools.name: preview_delete_blueprint_module
tools.description: Preview removing one module from a scenario's flow, without writing anything. Shows a state token that apply_delete_blueprint_module must be given unchanged.

module_id.description: The module's own id (module_id from get_scenario_blueprint) to remove.
module_id.title: Module Id

draft.description: True to preview against the draft version.
draft.title: Draft

tools.name: apply_delete_blueprint_module
tools.description: Apply a previously previewed module removal from a scenario. Re-reads the exact scenario blueprint and refuses to write if it changed since preview.

expected_state_token.description: Exact token from preview_delete_blueprint_module. Refuses to write if the blueprint changed since preview.
expected_state_token.title: Expected State Token

tools.name: list_organizations
tools.description: List the Make.com organizations the connected account belongs to -- the level above teams (an organization can contain several teams).

tools.name: list_team_members
tools.description: List the people with access to a Make team and their role -- Team Member, Team Admin, Team Monitoring, or a custom org role (shown by its numeric id).

TeamMember.description:
One user's access to a team. `role_name` is resolved for Make's own
built-in roles (Team Member/Team Admin/Team Monitoring); a custom org
role shows its raw numeric id instead since custom role names aren't
fetchable from this endpoint alone.
TeamMember.title: TeamMember

tools.name: list_api_tokens
tools.description: List the connected Make user's own API tokens -- label, scopes, creation date, and a masked form. Never exposes a usable secret; use create_api_token to mint a new one when a real value is needed.

MakeApiToken.description:
One of the CONNECTED user's own Make API tokens -- not the token
saved for this connector's own Make session (that one stays hidden as
always); `token` here is the last-4-chars-masked form Make itself
returns for existing tokens, so listing this never exposes a usable
secret.
MakeApiToken.title: MakeApiToken

tools.name: create_api_token
tools.description: Create a brand-new Make API token for the CONNECTED user's own account. The secret value is returned exactly ONCE, same as Make's own UI -- it cannot be retrieved again afterwards. This mints a real, usable credential -- treat it like creating a password.

label.description: Label shown in the Make user profile for this token.
label.title: Label

scope.description: Make API scopes to grant, e.g. ['scenarios:read','scenarios:write']. Full list via Make's own /enums/user-api-tokes-scopes.
scope.title: Scope

confirm.description: Must be true. This creates a real, usable Make credential -- treat it like any other secret.
confirm.title: Confirm

return_schema.description:
The newly created token's SECRET VALUE -- shown here exactly once,
same as Make's own UI. It is not retrievable again after this; if lost,
delete it and create a new one.
return_schema.title: CreatedApiToken

tools.name: delete_api_token
tools.description: Permanently delete one of the connected user's own Make API tokens. Anything using it (external scripts, other integrations) stops working immediately.

created_timestamp.description: The token's own 'created' timestamp from list_api_tokens (ISO 8601) -- Make identifies tokens by creation time, not a separate id.
created_timestamp.title: Created Timestamp

confirm.description: Must be true. Anything using this token stops working immediately.
confirm.title: Confirm

secrets.name: make_api_token
secrets.description: Your own Make.com API token, from Make: avatar (bottom-left) -> Profile -> API tab -> Add token.

secrets.name: make_zone
secrets.description: Auto-detected Make.com account zone (eu1/eu2/us1/us2) -- set automatically by connect_make, not entered manually.

secrets.name: make_webhook_url
secrets.description: Outgoing Make Custom Webhook trigger URL (from a Make scenario's Custom Webhook module) -- send_webhook_event POSTs to this. Independent of the make_api_token connection above.

panels.title: How to get a Make API token
